chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When God created the intellect, He said to it: 'Come forward!' So it came forward. Then He said to it: 'Turn back!' So it turned back. Then He said: 'By My Might and My Majesty! I have not created a creation better than you. To you I command, and to you I forbid, and to you I give reward, and to you I give punishment.'

key_terms.أَقْبِلْ / أَدْبِرْ: Come forward / Turn back — the divine test of the intellect's obedience, demonstrating its responsiveness to divine will
key_terms.الْعَقْل: al-Aql — the Intellect; in Shia theology, a cosmic principle and the highest of God's creations, the faculty through which humans are morally accountable
key_terms.وَعِزَّتِي وَجَلَالِي: By My Might and My Majesty — a divine oath formula emphasizing the gravity of the declaration

ai.seo_question: What did God say when He created the intellect according to Al-Kafi hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a cosmological account of the creation of the intellect (al-aql), one of the most celebrated narrations in the Kitab al-Aql of Al-Kafi. God addresses the intellect directly, testing its obedience and then declaring it the most noble of all creations, making it the exclusive subject of divine command, prohibition, reward, and punishment. This establishes the intellect's central role in moral and religious accountability in Shia theological thought.
